findings.title: Negative queryset slicing raises in Django, so the "advanced" path always 500s
findings.body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices the queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`). Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly rejects negative indices/slice bounds (`ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`), so the comment "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. Any request with a negative cursor offset on this code path results in an unhandled 500 rather than a 400/BadPaginationError. Negative cursor offsets are reachable because `Cursor.from_string` parses `int(bits[1])` without a sign check.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses integer key semantics on a datetime column
findings.body: The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime` (a `DateTimeField`) but the optimized branch passes `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator`, whose `get_item_key` does `int(math.floor(getattr(item, self.key)))` and whose `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value. `math.floor()` on a `datetime` raises `TypeError`, and feeding a raw integer cursor value into `build_queryset`'s `datetime >= %s` extra-where produces a SQL type error. The original code used `DateTimePaginator` precisely because the key needs the millisecond-multiplier conversion. As written, `?optimized_pagination=true` returns a 500 for any request that reaches this branch; there is no test covering it.

findings.title: Superuser check bypasses active-superuser verification and can crash on non-member actors
findings.body: `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is used to unlock the alternate pagination path. Two problems: (1) Sentry gates privileged behaviour on `is_active_superuser(request)` (which honours superuser session elevation / staff requirements), so reading `request.user.is_superuser` directly grants the privileged path to any account with the flag regardless of elevation state; (2) `organization_context.member` is `None` for requestors that are not org members (e.g. API-token/integration auth where `request.user` is anonymous), so evaluating `.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError` and returns a 500 on an otherwise valid request.

findings.title: BasePaginator silently clamps negative offsets and then uses the unclamped value
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` silently turns an invalid (negative) forward cursor offset into page 0 instead of failing with `BadPaginationError` as every other paginator in this module does, hiding malformed/tampered cursors from callers. Worse, the clamped value is only used for the slice: further down, the prev-page trim still compares `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` using the raw (possibly negative) `offset`, so the two values can disagree and the extra row is trimmed incorrectly. For `is_prev` cursors the negative offset is still passed straight into the slice and will raise in Django, so the clamp doesn't even fix the crash it appears to target.

findings.title: Span cap hardcoded to 1000 in Lua, ignoring SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans
findings.body: The new eviction logic hardcodes `1000` both as the threshold and as the retained size, while `SpansBuffer.__init__` still accepts `max_segment_spans` (default 1001) which is now referenced nowhere after the removal of the count check in `_load_segment_data`. The configuration knob is therefore dead and silently ineffective, and changing the limit requires editing the Lua script. The limit should be passed to the script as an ARGV value derived from `max_segment_spans`, and/or the unused constructor parameter removed.

findings.title: zunionstore defaults to AGGREGATE SUM, corrupting end-timestamp scores on merge
findings.body: `zunionstore` is called without `AGGREGATE`, so Redis sums the scores of members present in both source zsets. Since the score is `end_timestamp_precise` and used for eviction ordering (`zpopmin`), any span payload that exists in both the span's own set and the target set (e.g. a re-delivered/duplicated span, which the comments elsewhere acknowledge can happen when partitioning assumptions break) gets a score of roughly twice the timestamp. That span then sorts as the newest and is retained while genuinely newer spans are evicted. Use `AGGREGATE MIN` (or MAX) to keep scores meaningful.

findings.title: Span eviction is now silent: metric and error log for oversized segments were removed
findings.body: The previous code emitted `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` and logged an error when a segment exceeded the span-count limit. That branch is deleted and the new behaviour (dropping the oldest spans via `zpopmin` inside add-buffer.lua) emits no metric or log at all. Segments silently lose spans in production with no way to detect or quantify the data loss. Add a counter/metric for evicted spans (e.g. return the evicted count from the Lua script and record it).

findings.title: Redirect-chain limit lowered 10x without explanation
findings.body: The redirect-resolution loop bound was changed from `0, 10000` to `0, 1000` and the comment documenting the consequence ("segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly") was deleted. This is an unrelated, undocumented behaviour change: segment trees deeper than 1000 redirects will now be split into multiple segments instead of being joined. Either restore the previous bound or keep the comment and justify the new value.

findings.title: No test for the new in-insert eviction path
findings.body: The headline change of this PR is eviction during insert (set -> sorted set, `zpopmin` when a segment exceeds 1000 spans), but no test exercises a segment larger than the cap, verifies which spans are kept (newest by `end_timestamp_precise`), or verifies that scores survive the `zunionstore` merge path. All existing tests use 1-5 spans and therefore never reach the eviction branch, so a regression in the eviction arithmetic (`span_count - 1000`) or score handling would go unnoticed.

findings.title: New public paginator class has no tests and duplicates BasePaginator.get_result
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is added with no unit tests in `tests/sentry/api/test_paginator.py` even though it is wired into a production endpoint. Its `get_result` is a near-verbatim copy of `BasePaginator.get_result` with one extra branch, so any future fix to the base implementation (cursor trimming, hit counting) will silently not apply here. Prefer overriding only the offset computation, and add tests covering the forward, prev and negative-offset cases.

findings.title: Module docstring still describes Redis sets and omits the new span cap
findings.body: The module docstring (steps 3 and the glossary line "span-buf:s:* -- the actual set keys") still says spans are added to a Redis set, but the implementation now uses sorted sets keyed by `end_timestamp_precise`, and segments are capped at 1000 spans with the oldest evicted during insert. Someone reading this docstring will have the wrong model of both the data structure and the data-loss behaviour.

findings.title: Unguarded access to end_timestamp_precise can crash the consumer
findings.body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` is read with a hard subscript while every other field that may be absent uses `.get()`. If any message on `ingest-spans` lacks the field (older producer, replayed backlog, malformed payload) this raises `KeyError` inside `process_batch`, which fails the whole batch and puts the consumer into a crash loop rather than dropping or defaulting the single message. Consider defaulting (e.g. to the message timestamp) or explicitly rejecting the individual span.
